text:
jon-customer: Getting a bunch of 502s from your API and our billing jumped. We don't see any request IDs in our client logs. Can someone tell me what to send?

maria-support: Sorry about that — we can help. Quick ask: can you grab one example request (time window + request payload) and any request headers your client sent? The most useful bits are the Redwood request ID and the full response headers.

jon-customer: I tried but our mobile app log only shows the HTTP status and body. No 'x-redwood-request-id' header. Where should I look in the Console?

maria-support: In the Console go to Activity -> Requests, set the time range to when you saw the 502, filter by your org/project, then click a request row. The request detail modal shows: request_id, region, model, and raw request/response headers. Screenshot or copy that 'request_id' string. If you can't find it, still send the exact timestamp and client IP — we can correlate. :mag_right:

jon-customer: Okay found a time: 2025-07-20 16:12:43 UTC. No request_id in our app logs though.

sam-eng: Two quick ways to grab the ID from the client side: 1) If you can curl the endpoint, use -i to show headers, response will include x-redwood-request-id. Example minimal repro: 

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \-H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_KEY" \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Look for the header in the HTTP response: `x-redwood-request-id: <long-id>` or `x-request-id`. 2) In Node/JS fetch: `const rid = res.headers.get('x-redwood-request-id') || res.headers.get('x-request-id')`

sam-eng: If you use one of our SDKs, the response object often surfaces the id as `resp.request_id` or `resp.meta.request_id` depending on the language. For mobile SDKs check logs when DEBUG is enabled — search for "request_id" or "trace_id".

jon-customer: We're running through a CDN + auth proxy. Could that strip the header?

sam-eng: Yes, proxies can drop or rename headers. If you have a proxy, please capture a HAR (for browser) or a tcpdump/proxy access logs that include response headers. Alternatively, ask your infra to pass-through `x-redwood-request-id` or to log response headers. If proxy is rewriting, include the proxied request/response headers.

maria-support: Also helpful to include: account/org ID, the exact route (/v1/generate or /v1/embeddings), model name, SDK version, region, and approximate number of tokens. For billing spikes include the invoice ID or billing window and a screenshot of billing UI.

jon-customer: We can attach a HAR from a browser request and the mobile log snippet. Anything else?

sam-eng: Please also attach a minimal, sanitized curl that reproduces the 502 (replace keys and any PII). Example with traceparent (if you use distributed tracing):

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \-H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" \-d '{"input":"short prompt to reproduce"}'
```

sam-eng: If you can't share a repro, we can still trace server-side if you provide: exact timestamp(s) (UTC), client IP(s), organization ID, and any potential Request-IDs you found in proxies.

maria-support: If you want to include a debug bundle instead (recommended for mobile/embedded repros), create a debug bundle from the SDK/dev console with logs, config, and the failing payload. Label it with the timestamp. We will pull the server-side traces once we have the bundle.

jon-customer: Sending HAR + mobile snippets + sanitized curl now. Also attaching the billing screenshot (invoice # INV-2025-07-99).

maria-support: Received — thanks. We'll correlate on our side and ping back with the server request_id and debug findings. If we need a deeper trace we'll request a short window of packet capture or proxy logs. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: rollback-to-2025-07-20-15:50 (sha: a1b2c3) :truck:

maria-support: Noted — we see a transient backend error pattern around that time. We'll escalate to eng and share the server request id in this thread once we have it.

jon-customer: Thanks — appreciate the fast help.
